verdict.rationale: Viam documents agent-driven operation directly: an AI agent with a shell or an SDK can operate a machine like a person or program can. The CLI and machine API can call any method a machine serves and send commands remotely, including collision-checked motion via the motion service. Scoping is supported through per-resource, per-method `user_permissions` and fleet-level permission and authorization management. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of the agent's credential/API-key authentication flow, and independent or hands-on corroboration of an agent commanding real hardware end-to-end.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can have an AI agent authenticate with scoped credentials and command a real robot end-to-end through the platform's API or SDK

citations.quote: An AI agent with a shell or an SDK can operate a Viam machine the same way a person or a program can.
Machines can optionally enforce per-resource, per-method restrictions through `user_permissions` in the machine's JSON config
The machine API allows you to connect to your machine from within a supported Viam SDK, retrieve status information, and send commands remotely.
The CLI can call any API method a machine serves, with JSON in and JSON out. That makes it a complete way to operate a machine from a shell
